methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Design a 4-digit BCD up counter with synchronous reset.
The counter counts from 0000 to 9999 and wraps around to 0000.
Each decimal digit is encoded using 4 bits.
The counter has a synchronous active-high reset input.
ena[1] is the enable signal for the tens digit.
ena[2] is the enable signal for the hundreds digit.
ena[3] is the enable signal for the thousands digit.
Enable signals are asserted when all lower digits are 9.
Enable signals are synchronous and active-high.
spec_atomic_units: Module top_module has inputs clk and reset.
Module top_module has outputs ena[3:1] and q[15:0].
ena[1] is asserted when the ones digit q[3:0] reaches 9.
ena[2] is asserted when the ones and tens digits reach 9.
ena[3] is asserted when the ones, tens, and hundreds digits reach 9.
Comparators can be implemented using XOR gates and a NOR gate.
reset action occurs on the active edge of the clock.
The counter increments on the rising edge of clk.
When reset is high, the counter q is synchronously reset to 0.
All outputs change synchronously with the rising edge of clk.
The registers are updated on the positive edge of the clock (clk).
The q output is declared as reg [15:0] q, indicating that it holds its value between clock cycles.
The counter uses non-blocking assignments (<=) within an always @(posedge clk) block to update the register values.
ena signals are combinational outputs derived from the current state of q.
